metadata.description: A storage class — the named policy by which a platform provisions storage volumes. Models the construct that Kubernetes calls a StorageClass: a provisioner, a reclaim policy, volume binding mode, and provider-specific parameters (IOPS, encryption, replication). Storage.Volume references this type to declare what kind of storage it needs; placement and enrichment policies select the right storage class for a request based on its capabilities. Provider-specific because storage class semantics and parameters vary across provisioners.

context.purpose: Names a storage provisioning policy — provisioner, reclaim, binding mode, capabilities — that volumes request storage by.
context.plain_description: The Kubernetes StorageClass construct: a named policy — its `name` and `provisioner` are required — saying which provisioner builds volumes, what happens to data on release (`reclaim_policy`), when binding happens (`volume_binding_mode`, Kubernetes-cased: `Immediate` or `WaitForFirstConsumer`), whether volumes can grow (`allow_volume_expansion`), and what the class can do (`capabilities` — IOPS, encryption, replication, snapshots). A volume asks for storage by naming a class; placement policies select classes by capability. Provisioner-specific parameters ride along opaquely — the provisioner interprets them, the model does not.
use_when: You need volumes to request storage by named policy instead of naming backends.
You need placement to pick storage by advertised capability (encrypted, fast, replicated).
not_for: The volume itself — Storage.Volume references a class.
The backing storage system — Storage.Cluster; the class is the policy naming what the cluster serves.
Host-local pools — Storage.Pool; a class is a platform-level provisioning policy.
works_with: Storage.Volume — volumes declare their class by reference.
Storage.Cluster — the storage cluster backing the class.
Compute.VM — VM disks select a storage class.

adopts.role: named storage provisioning policy (provisioner, reclaimPolicy, volumeBindingMode, parameters)

lifecycle.decommission: Provider deletes the storage class. Existing volumes provisioned by this class are not affected — they retain their storage; new provisioning against this class is no longer possible.

name.description: The storage class name (e.g. 'ceph-rbd-fast', 'gp3-encrypted'). Unique within the cluster.

provisioner.description: The storage provisioner that handles volumes of this class (a CSI driver name, e.g. 'block.csi.example.com').

reclaim_policy.description: What happens to the underlying storage when a volume is released.

volume_binding_mode.description: When volume binding and provisioning occur — immediately at PVC creation or deferred until a consumer is scheduled.

allow_volume_expansion.description: Whether volumes of this class can be expanded after creation.

tier.description: The governed `storage_tier` this class satisfies (ADR-038 §2 vocabulary; each term denotes a requirements floor). Maintainer ruling 2026-08-02: a provider MAY expose storage classes, but MUST map each advertised class back to a tier so tier-authored intent (ADR-036: name-selectable, requirements-authoritative) resolves against class-based providers. The class chosen for a request is recorded consumer-side as a realized fact (e.g. a Storage.Layout entry's `storage_backing`), never in portable intent.

capabilities.description: Queryable capability advertisements for placement policies.

parameters.description: Provider-specific parameters passed to the provisioner (e.g., pool name, fsType, compression). Opaque to UDLM — the provisioner interprets them.

name.description: The realized storage class name — the string value that Storage.Volume.storage_class references.

relationships.name: storage_backend
relationships.description: The storage cluster that backs this class (e.g., a Ceph cluster, a NetApp filer).
